title: Waiver Decision Worksheet — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Household Income Test
content:
On Benefit Overpayment Accounts, the household income percent is the annual household income on the request divided by the poverty guideline for the household size on the request, times one hundred, rounded to two decimals; the poverty guideline for a household is the one-person guideline plus the per-additional-person amount for each member beyond the first.

## The decision

The waiver decision follows the household income percent: at or below the full-waiver percent the whole waivable principal is waived; above it and at or below the partial-waiver percent the waiver share of the waivable principal is waived, rounded to the cent, and the rest stays in recovery; above the partial-waiver percent nothing is waived and the request is denied.

A request is granted only when the amount waived is the whole unpaid principal; when an amount above zero but less than the whole unpaid principal is waived the request is partially granted and the rest of the principal stays in recovery; when nothing is waived the request is denied. On an overpayment whose classification is not waiver-eligible, the waived amount is zero.

## Defined amounts

- **Poverty guideline figures, full-waiver percent, partial-waiver percent**: those listed for the overpayment's classification in the waiver schedule.
- **Waiver share**: the classification's partial-waiver share from the waiver schedule. The waiver share never exceeds one.
- **Waivable principal**: the principal standing unpaid on the decision date: the principal assessed less the principal recovered by repayments, benefit offsets and tax refund intercepts and the principal removed by waiver, cancellation and write-off adjustments, plus the principal put back by returned repayments and refunds.

## Worksheet

| Line | Entry |
|---|---|
| 1 | Household size and annual household income on the request |
| 2 | Poverty guideline: one-person figure plus the per-member figure times (household size less one) |
| 3 | Household income percent: line 1 income divided by line 2, times one hundred, rounded to two decimals |
| 4 | Waivable principal |
| 5 | Amount waived: line 4 if line 3 is at or below the full-waiver percent; the waiver share times line 4, rounded to the cent, if line 3 is above it and at or below the partial-waiver percent; zero above the partial-waiver percent |
| 6 | Decision: granted, partially granted or denied, by comparing line 5 with the whole unpaid principal |

## Worked example (hypothetical household and balances)

A Non-Fraud Overpayment — Agency Error account with USD 2,400.00 of principal standing unpaid; a household of three. With the waiver schedule figures for that classification, the guideline is USD 15650.00 plus two times USD 5500.00, which is USD 26,650.00.

| Annual household income | Income percent | Amount waived | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| USD 50,000.00 | 187.62 | USD 2,400.00 | Granted |
| USD 62,000.00 | 232.65 | 50 percent of USD 2,400.00, USD 1,200.00 | Partially granted |
| USD 70,000.00 | 262.66 | Nothing | Denied |
